title: REST controllers and request mapping

richText: A web API lets a client send an HTTP request and receive an HTTP response.
An endpoint is a URL path and an HTTP method that the application handles.
Spring MVC sends a matching request to a method in a controller class.
@RestController marks a controller whose methods return response data.
It combines @Controller with @ResponseBody. @Controller alone can also handle requests, but a returned String can name a view instead of being response text.
Spring must discover the controller as a bean. Keep it in the application package or a package included in component scanning.
Map a request to a method
@RequestMapping on a class sets a shared path for its handler methods.
@GetMapping on a method handles GET requests at its path.
Spring combines the class path with the method path.
Use a mapping for a specific HTTP method. @RequestMapping without a method restriction can match different HTTP methods.

example.title: Return a greeting from a GET endpoint
description: Place this controller in a package scanned by a Spring Boot application with Spring MVC support.
explanation: @RestController makes the returned String the response body.
This endpoint returns text. @RestController does not make every return value JSON.

richText: A message converter writes a Java return value into the HTTP response body.
The available converters and the selected response content type determine the format.
JSON conversion, request bodies and response status codes are covered on their own pages.

summary: Handle an HTTP request with a controller, then map a path to a Java method.
